Each block included: (a) fixation baseline (20 s), (b) auditory and visual instruction (“Compassion” or “Reappraisal”; 3 s), (c) fixation cross (5–7 s), (d) 12 cycles of image presentation (Negative or Neutral; 12 s) and fixation inter-trial interval (5–11 s, randomized), and (f) final baseline (17–38 s).
Participants were instructed to view the images and regulate their emotional responses

instructions.value: Participants viewed images for 12 seconds while employing their assigned strategy. Compassion trainees were instructed to evoke compassion while silently repeating compassion-generating phrases. Reappraisal trainees were instructed to decrease negative emotions by silently reinterpreting the emotional meaning of the images, such as viewing the scene as fake or not real or imagining a better outcome. Attend blocks required participants not to change their emotional response.

spans.text: Compassion trainees were instructed to evoke feelings of compassion while silently repeating compassion-generating phrases. In contrast, Reappraisal trainees were instructed to decrease negative emotions by silently re-interpreting the emotional meaning of the images

stimuli.value: Images depicting human suffering or non-suffering from the International Affective Picture System. Negative images depicted emotional distress, physical pain, or violence; neutral images depicted people in non-emotional situations such as working or walking on a street.
